summary: The former editorial node passage_aug_lib_arb_1_11_21 claimed that Augustine coined liberum arbitrium and was snapshot-linked both to the exact Latin locus and to a second synthetic corpus row with CTS 3.7.21. The synthesis and wrong corpus row are quarantined; the continuous Latin node is now the sole snapshot twin and valid graph references point to it.
resolution_criteria: The exact Latin node remains the sole snapshot for c91f039f-2616-4c5c-ba9c-822e459d08b5; the synthetic d4ed passage and false coinage wording never re-enter queryable data; Tertullian's earlier attestation remains explicit; targeted and global no-growth gates pass.

adjudication.decision: Quarantine the editorial synthesis and its wrong-CTS corpus twin; retain and hash the continuous Latin 1.11.21 text as the only snapshot.
adjudication.rationale: The primary Latin text supports Augustine's argument about the mind's own will and free choice, not a claim that he coined the phrase. Tertullian, Adversus Marcionem II.6, is earlier; a modern source-specific analysis also rejects reading the phrase as a brand-new faculty notion.
